lessons.title: Greetings & Introductions
lessons.description: Greet people, say your name, nationality and job, and ask simple yes/no questions.
lessons.topic: Meeting someone for the first time
objectives: Greet someone politely and introduce yourself
State your nationality and occupation with は and です
Ask and answer simple yes/no questions with か

vocabularyTargets.english: nice to meet you (said at a first meeting)

vocabularyTargets.japanese: よろしくお願いします
vocabularyTargets.reading: よろしくおねがいします
vocabularyTargets.english: pleased to meet you / I look forward to working with you

grammarTargets.name: A は B です
grammarTargets.explanation: は marks the topic (what we are talking about); です is the polite copula, roughly 'is/am/are'. Word order is topic – comment – です. は is written with the kana ha but pronounced wa as a particle.

grammarTargets.name: か questions and はい / いいえ
grammarTargets.explanation: Adding か to the end of a polite sentence turns it into a yes/no question; intonation can rise, but か alone already marks the question. Answer with はい、そうです or いいえ、ちがいます.

lessons.teachingNotes: Keep everything in polite style; strangers meeting for the first time would not use casual speech. Do not introduce です negatives yet beyond the fixed ちがいます.

lessons.title: People & Relationships
lessons.description: Talk about the people around you and connect nouns with の.
objectives: Name close family members and colleagues
Express possession and affiliation with の
Say 'also' with も

grammarTargets.name: の: possession and affiliation
grammarTargets.explanation: の links two nouns: the first describes or owns the second. 私の友達 = my friend; 会社の同僚 = a colleague from the company. The order is the reverse of English 'of'.

grammarTargets.name: も: also, too
grammarTargets.explanation: も replaces は (or が) to mean 'also'. It attaches to the noun that is 'also' true.

lessons.teachingNotes: 父/母/兄/妹 are humble forms for one's own family. Mention briefly that someone else's family uses お父さん/お母さん, but do not teach the full honorific system. Casual speech between friends may drop です (e.g. 友達。/ 誰？); keep casual lines short and justified by a friendly context.

lessons.title: Numbers & Prices
lessons.description: Count from 0 to 100, ask prices and point at things with これ・それ・あれ.
objectives: Recognise numbers 0–100
Ask 'how much is this?' and understand the answer
Distinguish これ / それ / あれ by distance

grammarTargets.name: いくらですか
grammarTargets.explanation: いくら means 'how much (money)'. Ask with N は いくらですか and answer with number + 円 です. Zero is ゼロ. Tens are built by multiplication then addition: 二十 (に・じゅう) = 20, 二十五 = 25.

grammarTargets.name: これ・それ・あれ
grammarTargets.explanation: これ = this (near me), それ = that (near you), あれ = that over there (far from both). They stand alone as pronouns; どれ asks 'which one'.

lessons.teachingNotes: Teach 四 = よん and 七 = なな as the default readings; mention し/しち exist but avoid them. 100 is ひゃく (not いちひゃく). Prices above 100 can appear only as recognisable numbers if needed (e.g. 三百 = さんびゃく is an irregular sound change — avoid unless explained).

lessons.title: Days, Dates & Time
lessons.description: Talk about days of the week and times, and ask when something happens.
objectives: Name the days of the week
Tell the time in hours and minutes
Use に with specific times and ask いつ / 何時

grammarTargets.name: Time + に
grammarTargets.explanation: Specific points in time (clock times, days of the week) take に when they modify a verb: 三時に起きます. With です alone, no に is needed: 会議は三時です. Relative words such as 今日, 明日 and 今 never take に. Verbs come in lesson 7, so here notice the pattern in listening only.
examples: パーティーは七時です。

grammarTargets.name: いつ / 何時
grammarTargets.explanation: いつ asks 'when' in general; 何時 (なんじ) asks 'what time'. 今、何時ですか = What time is it now?

lessons.teachingNotes: Dates of the month (ついたち, ふつか …) are highly irregular — defer them; this lesson covers weekdays and clock time only. Irregular hours: 四時 = よじ, 七時 = しちじ, 九時 = くじ. Minutes alternate ふん/ぷん (五分 ごふん, 十分 じゅっぷん); teach 五分, 十分, 三十分 (さんじゅっぷん) and 半 (はん, half past) as recognisable forms. Verbs have not been taught yet: use only です sentences.

lessons.title: Objects Around Us
lessons.description: Name everyday objects, describe their colour and point to specific things with この・その・あの.
objectives: Name ten everyday objects
Use この・その・あの before a noun
Ask 何ですか and describe colours

grammarTargets.name: この・その・あの + noun
grammarTargets.explanation: この/その/あの must be followed by a noun (この本 = this book), while これ/それ/あれ stand alone (これ = this one). Same distance logic: near me / near you / far from both.
examples: あのかばんは赤いです。

grammarTargets.name: 何ですか / noun + です
grammarTargets.explanation: 何ですか asks 'what is it?'. 何 is read なん before です and most counters. Colour words like 赤い can stand before a noun (赤いかばん) or at the end before です (かばんは赤いです).

lessons.teachingNotes: Colours appear here as fixed chunks; the full い-adjective system (negatives, past) comes in lessons 12–13. 誰の (whose) is a natural extension of の from lesson 2.

lessons.title: Places & Directions
lessons.description: Ask where places are and say what is where with あります and います.
objectives: Ask where something is with どこ
Use ここ・そこ・あそこ
Describe location with あります / います and position words

grammarTargets.name: ここ・そこ・あそこ / どこ
grammarTargets.explanation: Place words matching これ・それ・あれ: ここ = here, そこ = there (near you), あそこ = over there. どこ = where. トイレはどこですか = Where is the toilet?

grammarTargets.name: Place に あります / います
grammarTargets.explanation: Existence: inanimate things あります, living people and animals います. Place takes に. Position words attach with の: 机の上に = on the desk.
examples: 机の上に本があります。
銀行の隣にコンビニがあります。

lessons.teachingNotes: が appears for the first time as the subject marker in existence sentences; explain it only as 'marks what exists' and contrast briefly with は (topic). Casual: friends might say 猫がいる？ — this uses the dictionary form; keep any casual line to a single recognisable exchange, or omit.

lessons.title: Daily Activities
lessons.description: Describe everyday actions with polite verbs and mark objects with を.
objectives: Use common verbs in polite present affirmative and negative
Mark direct objects with を
Describe a daily routine with times

grammarTargets.name: 〜ます / 〜ません
grammarTargets.explanation: Polite non-past verbs end in ます (affirmative) and ません (negative). Non-past covers habits and the future: 毎日起きます = I get up every day. Only the ます form is taught here; dictionary forms come later.

grammarTargets.name: を: the direct object
grammarTargets.explanation: を marks what the action is done to. Japanese verbs come last: object を verb. を is pronounced o.

lessons.teachingNotes: Now that verbs exist, time + に can be practised properly (七時に起きます). Do not introduce the past tense (lesson 11) or the て-form (lesson 15).

lessons.title: Food & Drinks
lessons.description: Talk about food and drinks, say what you like, and ask for things politely.
lessons.topic: What you like to eat and drink
objectives: Name common foods and drinks
Say what you like and dislike with が好きです
Ask for something with をください

grammarTargets.name: 〜が好きです
grammarTargets.explanation: The thing liked is marked with が, not を: 魚が好きです = I like fish. Negative: 好きじゃないです (casual: 好きじゃない). あまり好きじゃないです softens it.
examples: 私はコーヒーが好きです。
肉はあまり好きじゃないです。

grammarTargets.name: 〜をください
grammarTargets.explanation: N をください = Please give me N. Polite and common in shops; お願いします is slightly softer.

lessons.teachingNotes: 好き is a な-adjective, but present it as a fixed pattern here; な-adjectives are systematised in lesson 12. A casual exchange between friends (魚、好き？ / うん、好き！) is natural.

lessons.title: At a Restaurant
lessons.description: Order food in a restaurant, count items and people, and ask for the bill.
objectives: Count things with the general counter 〜つ (1–5)
Count people with 一人 / 二人 / 〜人
Order and ask for the bill politely

grammarTargets.name: Counters: 〜つ and 〜人
grammarTargets.explanation: Japanese counts with counters. The native counter 〜つ counts most things (1–10); 一人 and 二人 are irregular, from three people on use number + 人 (三人 = さんにん). Word order: noun を number verb — コーヒーを二つください.
examples: コーヒーを二つください。

grammarTargets.name: 〜をお願いします
grammarTargets.explanation: N をお願いします is a soft, polite way to order or request. お会計をお願いします = The bill, please.
examples: お会計をお願いします。

lessons.teachingNotes: Counter scaffolding: only two counter systems are taught (〜つ for things, 〜人 for people). Do not introduce 〜本, 〜枚, 〜杯 etc. Staff speech such as 何名様ですか is honorific: present at most once, immediately followed by a plain explanation; the learner's own lines stay in simple polite style.

lessons.title: Going Somewhere
lessons.description: Say where you are going, coming and returning, and how you travel.
objectives: Use 行きます / 来ます / 帰ります with destinations
Mark the destination with へ or に
Mark the means of transport with で

grammarTargets.name: Destination へ / に
grammarTargets.explanation: Motion verbs take the destination with へ (direction, pronounced e) or に (arrival point). Both are natural with 行きます・来ます・帰ります.

grammarTargets.name: で: means of transport
grammarTargets.explanation: で marks the means: 電車で行きます = go by train. 'On foot' is 歩いて without で.
examples: バスで学校へ行きます。
飛行機で東京に来ます。

lessons.teachingNotes: 歩いて is technically a て-form; present it as a fixed adverb now and point back to it in lesson 15. Contrast で (means) with に/へ (destination) using pairs that change one element.

lessons.title: Past Experiences
lessons.description: Talk about what you did yesterday, last week and last year.
objectives: Use polite past affirmative and negative verbs
Use past time words
Say you did nothing with 何も〜ませんでした

grammarTargets.name: 〜ました / 〜ませんでした
grammarTargets.explanation: Polite past: replace ます with ました (did) and ません with ませんでした (did not). Works for every verb learned so far.
examples: 先週、友達に会いました。
昨日は学校へ行きませんでした。

grammarTargets.name: 何も + negative
grammarTargets.explanation: 何も with a negative verb means 'nothing'. 何も買いませんでした = I bought nothing.
examples: 何も食べませんでした。
昨日は何もしませんでした。

lessons.teachingNotes: 会います takes に for the person (友達に会います) — flag this as a common learner error. Casual past (見た, 行った) requires the た-form and is NOT taught yet: casual lines, if any, should avoid verb past forms (e.g. 映画？ / うん、面白かった would be too early — avoid).

lessons.title: Describing Things
lessons.description: Describe people, places and things with い- and な-adjectives.
objectives: Use い-adjectives before nouns and at the end of sentences
Use な-adjectives with な before nouns
Form polite negatives of both adjective types

grammarTargets.name: い-adjectives
grammarTargets.explanation: い-adjectives end in い and go straight before nouns (高い本) or before です (この本は高いです). Negative: replace い with くないです (高くないです). Irregular: いい → よくないです.
examples: あの映画は面白くないです。

grammarTargets.name: な-adjectives
grammarTargets.explanation: な-adjectives take な before a noun (静かな部屋) and です at the end (部屋は静かです). Negative: じゃないです. Warning: きれい ends in い but is a な-adjective.
examples: この部屋は静かじゃないです。

lessons.teachingNotes: Present adjective negatives as polite 〜くないです / 〜じゃないです (the 〜くありません form can be mentioned as more formal). Casual: drop です (高い！ / 静かだね). Past of adjectives comes in lesson 13.

lessons.title: Weather & Seasons
lessons.description: Make small talk about the weather and seasons, now and in the past.
objectives: Ask and answer どうですか questions
Describe weather with adjectives
Use the past of adjectives (〜かったです / 〜でした)

grammarTargets.name: どうですか + adjective predicates
grammarTargets.explanation: 〜はどうですか asks 'how is …?' and invites an adjective answer: 天気はどうですか → 寒いです. Noun weather words take です: 雨です.
examples: 今日の天気はどうですか。
東京の夏はとても暑いです。

grammarTargets.name: Past of adjectives
grammarTargets.explanation: い-adjectives: 〜い → 〜かったです (寒かったです). な-adjectives and nouns: 〜でした (静かでした, 雨でした). Irregular: いい → よかったです.
examples: 去年の冬は暖かかったです。

lessons.teachingNotes: Weather small talk often uses ね (暑いですね) — introduce ね as a rapport particle ('isn't it'). Casual: 寒いね！/ 寒かったね is natural between friends. Do not confuse pitch accent with sentence intonation: rising intonation on どう？ is intonation.

lessons.title: Shopping
lessons.description: Shop for clothes, say what you want and compare two items.
objectives: Say what you want with 〜がほしいです
Compare two things with より and のほうが
Ask about size and colour

grammarTargets.name: 〜がほしいです
grammarTargets.explanation: ほしい is an い-adjective meaning 'want (a thing)'. The thing wanted takes が: 新しい靴がほしいです. Used for the speaker's own wishes; for others it is avoided.
examples: 新しいシャツがほしいです。
もっと小さいサイズがほしいです。

grammarTargets.name: A は B より 〜です / どちらが
grammarTargets.explanation: A は B より adjective です = A is more … than B. Ask with A と B と どちらが 〜ですか and answer with 〜のほうが 〜です.
examples: このシャツはあのシャツより安いです。
黒と白とどちらがいいですか。

lessons.teachingNotes: Keep shop staff speech in simple polite style (no お客様 / ございます chains). と for 'and' between nouns appears in the comparison question; flag it briefly.

lessons.title: Work & Office
lessons.description: Make polite requests at work and learn how the て-form is built.
objectives: Recognise how the て-form is formed from the ます-stem
Make polite requests with 〜てください
Understand common office vocabulary

grammarTargets.name: The て-form (from the ます-stem)
grammarTargets.explanation: Remove ます and look at the last sound. Group 2: just add て (食べ→食べて, 見せ→見せて). Irregular: し→して, 来→きて. Group 1: い/ち/り→って (待ち→待って, 送り→送って, 手伝い→手伝って); み/び/に→んで (読み→読んで, 飲み→飲んで); き→いて (書き→書いて, 聞き→聞いて); ぎ→いで; し→して. Exception: 行き→行って.

grammarTargets.name: 〜てください
grammarTargets.explanation: て-form + ください = please do …. Add ちょっと or 少し to soften. Recall 歩いて from lesson 10 — it was a て-form all along.
examples: 資料を見せてください。
後でメールを送ってください。

lessons.teachingNotes: SCAFFOLDING: the て-form is the hardest morphology so far. Step 5 should build it in three passes (group 2 + irregular → group 1 っ/ん → group 1 い/いで + 行って), with 2–3 examples each, not one rushed table. Pattern variation should keep the verb fixed and change the object, then keep the object and change the verb. Lessons 16–19 reuse the て-form.

lessons.title: Plans & Invitations
lessons.description: Invite someone, accept or politely decline, and suggest doing things together.
objectives: Invite with 〜ませんか
Suggest with 〜ましょう / 〜ましょうか
Decline politely with ちょっと…

grammarTargets.name: 〜ませんか (invitation)
grammarTargets.explanation: A negative question used as a gentle invitation: 一緒に行きませんか = Won't you come with me? It leaves room to refuse, so it is more polite than ましょう.
examples: 今晩、一緒に映画を見ませんか。
土曜日に散歩しませんか。
いいですね。行きましょう。

grammarTargets.name: 〜ましょう / 〜ましょうか
grammarTargets.explanation: 〜ましょう = let's …; 〜ましょうか = shall we …? / shall I …?. Polite refusal: ちょっと… or 残念ですが、〜は約束があります.
examples: 何時に会いましょうか。
七時に駅で会いましょう。
残念ですが、来週はちょっと…。

lessons.teachingNotes: Casual invitations (行かない？ / 行こう) need the ない-form and volitional form, not yet taught: keep this lesson polite. で for the place of an action (駅で会いましょう) appears; explain briefly and contrast with に for existence.

lessons.title: Abilities & Preferences
lessons.description: Talk about what you can do, your hobbies and how well you do things; meet the dictionary form.
objectives: Say what you can do with できます and ことができます
Form the dictionary form from the ます form
Talk about skill with 上手 / 下手

grammarTargets.name: Noun が できます / Dictionary form + ことができます
grammarTargets.explanation: できます = can do. With a noun: 日本語ができます. With a verb: dictionary form + ことができます. Dictionary form from ます-stem: group 1 i→u (泳ぎ→泳ぐ, 弾き→弾く, 歌い→歌う), group 2 add る (食べ→食べる), irregular します→する, 来ます→来る.
examples: ピアノを弾くことができます。
全然泳ぐことができません。

grammarTargets.name: 上手 / 下手 + が
grammarTargets.explanation: Skill: person は thing が 上手です. Saying 上手です about yourself sounds boastful; the modest reply to a compliment is いいえ、まだまだです.

lessons.teachingNotes: This is the first formal introduction of the dictionary form: make the ます ↔ dictionary pairs explicit and contrast them, using verbs from lessons 7, 10, 11 and 15. Casual: friends use the dictionary form directly (泳げる？ is the potential form — do NOT use; prefer 泳ぐ？ only as 'do you swim?').

lessons.title: Health & Wellbeing
lessons.description: Describe how you feel and simple symptoms, and meet the casual negative ない-form.
objectives: Name body parts and describe pain with 〜が痛いです
Understand simple symptoms and advice
Form and use the casual negative ない-form

grammarTargets.name: Body part が 痛いです
grammarTargets.explanation: Pain: body part + が 痛いです = My … hurts. 熱があります = I have a fever; 風邪をひきました = I caught a cold (fixed phrase). Ask: 大丈夫ですか.

grammarTargets.name: The ない-form (casual negative)
grammarTargets.explanation: Casual negative of verbs. Group 1: change the ending to the あ-row + ない (休む→休まない, 飲む→飲まない; う→わない: 歌う→歌わない). Group 2: drop る + ない (食べる→食べない). Irregular: する→しない, 来る→こない.
examples: 今日は仕事に行かない。
大丈夫？ — うん、大丈夫。

lessons.teachingNotes: Present the ない-form after a recap of dictionary forms from lesson 17. Casual exchanges belong to friends or family checking on each other; the doctor/clinic exchange stays polite. Keep medical content non-diagnostic and everyday.

lessons.title: Travel & Accommodation
lessons.description: Check in at a hotel, ask for permission and understand what is not allowed.
objectives: Ask for permission with 〜てもいいですか
Understand prohibitions with 〜てはいけません
Handle a simple hotel check-in and a small problem

vocabularyTargets.english: be in trouble, have a problem

grammarTargets.name: 〜てもいいですか (permission)
grammarTargets.explanation: て-form + もいいですか = May I …? Answer はい、どうぞ or すみません、ちょっと….
examples: 荷物を預けてもいいですか。
ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか。

grammarTargets.name: 〜てはいけません (prohibition)
grammarTargets.explanation: て-form + はいけません = must not …. Strong; common on signs and rules. Polite refusal to a request uses ちょっと… instead.
examples: ここでたばこを吸ってはいけません。
部屋で料理をしてはいけません。

lessons.teachingNotes: Re-scaffold the て-form with a 60-second recap before teaching もいい / はいけない. Casual ～ちゃだめ is recognition-only at most; prefer to omit.

lessons.title: Integrated Conversations
lessons.description: Review the main themes in longer natural conversations and link sentences smoothly.
objectives: Follow a longer conversation mixing earlier topics
Link ideas with でも・それから・だから
Choose polite or casual register appropriately

vocabularyTargets.japanese: ありがとうございました
vocabularyTargets.reading: ありがとうございました

vocabularyTargets.english: thank you for your hard work

grammarTargets.name: Linking sentences: でも・それから・だから
grammarTargets.explanation: Start a new sentence with でも (contrast), それから (sequence) or だから (reason → result) to connect ideas without new grammar.
examples: 昨日は雨でした。でも、楽しかったです。
映画を見ました。それから、レストランへ行きました。
熱があります。だから、今日は休みます。

grammarTargets.name: Choosing register
grammarTargets.explanation: Polite (です/ます) with strangers, colleagues and staff; casual with friends and family. Characters should switch only when the relationship justifies it.
examples: 本当にありがとうございました。

lessons.teachingNotes: This lesson has few new words on purpose. Build Step 1 as a longer dialogue (up to 7 turns) between two colleagues who become friendlier; Step 11 can be a casual phone call between friends planning the weekend. No new grammar beyond the linking words.
